exposure: Subpopulation 1:  126,620 fresh cycles and subsequent frozen embryo transfers between 2007 and 2019

BMI categorized according to the World Health Organization as underweight (<18.5), normal weight (18.5-24.9, reference), overweight (25.0-29.9), class I obesity (30.0-34.9), class II obesity (35.0-39.9), and class III obesity (>=40.0)
outcome: cumulative live birth per started fresh IVF cycle, including fresh and subsequent frozen embryo transfers
preterm birth at less than 37 weeks
cohort: Women undergoing IVF between 2002 and 2020 in a national, population-based cohort.
finding: The cumulative live birth rate decreased significantly with increasing BMI, while the risk of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, preterm birth, and other perinatal complications, such as perinatal death, increased significantly and progressively with increasing BMI.
